rfm_tuples.M_value: Three separate Item 5.02 departure 8-Ks in a 9-week window: (1) Oct 15, 2025 (accession 0000860748-25-000198) — CEO Joseph P. Thomas Evans, Jr. (66, General Counsel since 1992) appointed Interim CEO; Board still 'initiating' a search via 'a leading global executive search firm'. (2) Oct 24, 2025 — Chief Claims Officer P&C Duane A. Sanders terminated WITHOUT CAUSE effective Oct 22, 2025 ($2.025M severance disclosed Dec 19). (3) Nov 10, 2025 (acc 0000860748-25-000225) — $2.225M of retention RSUs granted to CFO Camden ($775K), CIO Boschelli ($675K), and Kemper Auto President Hunton ($775K), plus a separate retention award to the Interim CEO (8-K/A Nov 7), explicitly to retain executives 'following the recently announced leadership changes'. claim_evolution: 4/4 AFFIRMED — Interim CEO Evans still signing 10-Q certifications May 6, 2026, i.e., 7 months post-departure with no permanent CEO. The 10-K (filed Feb 11, 2026) Item 1 narrative makes ZERO mention of the CEO departure, the without-cause termination, or the open search. Item 9 says 'Not Applicable'. The only acknowledgment is the cover-page Principal Executive Officer signature by 'Interim' Evans.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Calibrated obscuring. The 10-K is filed 17 weeks AFTER the CEO termination-without-cause and 17 weeks AFTER the Chief Claims Officer termination-without-cause, yet the Item 1 business narrative reads as if leadership is stable. Two C-suite without-cause terminations in 8 days plus $5.72M + $2.025M severance plus $2.225M+ retention RSUs to remaining executives, plus a still-open CEO search seven months later, is a discontinuity that would normally be flagged in the MD&A 'Summary of Results' and 'Critical Accounting Estimates' sections. Burying it as a signature-block change while running a glossy 'leading specialized insurer' narrative is OBSCURING in the strict HONESTY-ALPHA sense. The without-cause framing (vs 'mutual agreement' / 'pursuing other opportunities') is itself revealing: the Board affirmatively chose the more litigation-protective path, then signed away $5.72M of severance to make it stick. This pattern is the classic 'Board lost confidence' signature.

rfm_tuples.M_value: 63% California concentration in a non-standard auto book is extreme — and the 10-K explicitly admits 'Because of restrictions placed on the Company's ability to increase premium rates in certain states, including California, a pricing inadequacy may continue for a prolonged period. These pricing inadequacies have had a material impact on the Company's operating results in recent periods and may impact operating results in future periods.' (Item 1A). Cat reinsurance is $50M retention with only 95% coverage above — so a $200M cat event costs Kemper $50M + 5%*$110M + everything above $160M. Property & Casualty Insurance Reserves rose from $2,621.3M (12/31/24) to $2,940.3M (12/31/25), a $318.9M (+12%) increase; Personal Auto reserves alone rose $200.8M (+12.4%) and Commercial Auto reserves rose $220.7M (+30.6%) — disproportionate reserve build vs single-digit premium growth (P&C NWP $4,013M vs $3,837M, +4.6%). The Critical Audit Matter is precisely the P&C reserve estimation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'managed via diversification and reinsurance' framing is materially weak when 63% of segment premium is in one rate-restricted state with the company itself admitting the pricing inadequacy may persist. The 30.6% YoY Commercial Auto reserve build in a year where commercial auto NWP grew 22.7% ($797.7M -> $978.7M) is a tell: reserves growing faster than written premium in a long-tail line is the canonical reserve-strengthening fingerprint. The Critical Audit Matter on P&C reserves is Deloitte's tacit acknowledgement that the actuarial estimate is at high risk of adverse development. The CFO Camden signing as PEO at the Q1-2026 8-K and the Chief Claims Officer being terminated 12 weeks earlier (C2) connects to this: claims/reserve leadership turned over precisely when reserves are inflating.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Sequence: Aug 5 — Board approves $500M new buyback. Aug 13 — $150M ASR with GS; 2,279,203 initial shares delivered Aug 14 at implied price ~$66. Oct 2025 — additional 1,655,662 shares repurchased at avg $48.07 = $79.6M (10-K Item 5 table). Nov & Dec 2025 — ZERO shares repurchased ($304.2M authorization untouched). Then: Oct 14 — CEO Lacher terminated without cause. Oct 22 — Chief Claims Officer terminated without cause. Nov 4 — retention RSUs granted to remaining C-suite. Net Cash Used in Financing Activities = $860.1M in 2025 vs $137.2M in 2024 (+$722.9M), driven by buybacks + redemption of $450M 4.350% senior notes. Stock price fell from ~$66 (Aug ASR) to $48 (Oct repurchases) to ~$38 (Feb 2026 insider Form 4s) to $34.24 (Feb 6, 2026). The $150M ASR was effectively underwater by ~40% within 60 days.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The timing pattern is sharply asymmetric to the company's narrative. A new $500M buyback announced Aug 5, then a $150M ASR raced into market Aug 13 — eight weeks before the Board terminates its CEO without cause. The Board does not terminate a CEO without cause without weeks of deliberation; the loss-of-confidence trajectory almost certainly predated the ASR. Buying back $230M of stock immediately before two without-cause C-suite terminations and a Q4 result that drove the stock to $38 means shareholders financed an ASR at $66 that was worth $38 four months later. The November/December zero-buyback gap inside the same 'aggressive' repurchase quarter is the giveaway: capital return discipline halted exactly when MNPI risk peaked. The 10-K narrative does not connect these dots.

Critical Audit Matter is P&C insurance reserves — specifically calling out 'a high degree of auditor judgment and an increased extent of effort, including the need to involve our actuarial specialists', and that Deloitte developed an INDEPENDENT range of estimates and compared the prior-year estimates to actual to test for management bias. Critical Accounting Estimates also list: valuation of investments (with $343.6M Level 3 fixed maturities, of which 92% are broker/dealer-quoted with 'lack of transparency'), life insurance reserves, goodwill ($1.0B+ implied), and DTA recoverability (NOLs $18.8M, valuation allowance $38.0M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The audit opinion is clean and the controls assertion is standard. The flag here is the Critical Audit Matter wording: Deloitte explicitly developed an INDEPENDENT estimate range and tested for prior-year bias — that is the language auditors use when they have a documented disagreement on assumptions that was resolved within tolerance. Paired with C3 (12% reserve build vs 4.6% NWP growth, 30.6% commercial-auto reserve build) and C2 (Chief Claims Officer terminated without cause one month before audit completion), the CAM is doing more work than the boilerplate suggests. MODERATE because the opinion stands; the qualitative read of the CAM points to elevated restatement-adjacent risk.

rfm_tuples.R: Kemper Reciprocal (Illinois-domiciled reciprocal insurance exchange established Q3 2023) is a routine policyholder-owned vehicle managed by a Kemper-owned attorney-in-fact (AIF), with the AIF entitled to up to 30% management fee on gross written premium. Net written premium reported through the Exchange was $50.3M in 2025 (vs $27.6M in 2024 and $0.6M in 2023).
rfm_tuples.f: If true: the Exchange should function as a transparent, arm's-length structure with no off-balance-sheet risk concentration; growth should be measured and consistent with the disclosed reciprocal-exchange model; structure should not be used as a regulatory-arbitrage vehicle for distressed business.

rfm_tuples.M_value: edgar_fts: 42 total hits, top filings dominated by Kemper's own quarterly earnings releases and 10-K/10-Q (no third-party validation). Reciprocal Exchange consolidated as a VIE per the 10-K. P&C reserves attributable to Kemper Reciprocal: $29.4M at 12/31/25 vs $9.4M at 12/31/24 (+213% YoY). Premium grew from $0.6M (2023) to $27.6M (2024) to $50.3M (2025) — 83x in two years. AIF management fee is up to 30% of gross written premium, paid to a Kemper-owned subsidiary — i.e., Kemper extracts management economics regardless of the Exchange's underwriting profitability. The Exchange is the vehicle through which 'subscribers' (policyholders) absorb underwriting risk while Kemper books the fee. Bermuda subsidiary reports $66.9M pre-tax income vs $93.8M for the US — 41% of pre-tax income is offshore.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Reciprocal Exchange is disclosed as required and the structure is legal and not uncommon in non-standard auto, but the 83x premium growth in 24 months in a segment where the parent company is having reserve adequacy concerns (C3) and just terminated its Chief Claims Officer (C2) deserves scrutiny. Reciprocal exchanges are a known mechanism for moving distressed personal lines premium off the holding company's loss-ratio-bearing balance sheet while retaining fee economics. The fee-extraction model means a Kemper subsidiary earns up to 30% of GWP whether or not subscribers ultimately lose money. The Bermuda 41% pre-tax-income share is a separate calibrated-disclosure point that the 10-K narrative does not foreground in MD&A. MODERATE because the structure is legal and disclosed in the notes; the framing in Item 1 understates the strategic importance of the vehicle as a risk-shifting tool.

summary: KMPR presents as a stable, ongoing specialty auto + life insurer with clean GAAP, clean auditor, no going-concern issues, and a continuous dividend. The disclosed facts reveal a different picture: (a) the CEO was terminated WITHOUT CAUSE on Oct 14, 2025 (with $5.72M severance + accelerated equity), the Chief Claims Officer was terminated WITHOUT CAUSE on Oct 22, 2025 ($2.025M severance), and a 7-month-and-counting interim period followed — yet the 10-K Item 1 business narrative and Item 9 ('Not Applicable') do not flag this as a material discontinuity; (b) the Board approved a NEW $500M buyback Aug 5, then executed a $150M ASR Aug 13 (eight weeks before firing the CEO), with the stock then falling 42% by early Feb 2026 — the ASR was effectively underwater within 60 days; (c) Lacher's $4.5M tax-vesting sale on Sept 10, 2025 at $52.96 (vs $34 by Feb 6, 2026) was 34 days before his without-cause termination; (d) P&C reserves grew 12% on 4.6% premium growth, with commercial auto reserves up 30.6% — the Critical Audit Matter explicitly describes Deloitte building an independent reserve range and testing for management bias; (e) 63% of Specialty P&C premium is California, where the 10-K admits pricing inadequacy 'may continue for a prolonged period'; (f) Kemper Reciprocal grew 83x in 2 years to $50M NWP with up to 30% AIF fee extraction by a Kemper subsidiary — a fee-positive risk-shifting vehicle; (g) 41% of pre-tax income is booked through Bermuda. The HONESTY-ALPHA case is calibrated obscuring, not outright fraud: each individual fact is technically disclosed somewhere (Item 5.02 8-Ks, Note 22, Item 1A), but the 10-K's Item 1 narrative and the Item 9 'Not Applicable' representation paint a continuity story that the underlying disclosures contradict. This is a credit-event / reserve-strengthening / governance-vacuum LONG-from-the-trough screen, but not a clean rebound: the calibrated obscuring of the CEO transition is the dominant signal.
